name: Key Utility Questions for Your Los Angeles ADU Design Contractor

mainEntity.name: What should I ask an ADU design contractor about utility upgrades and capacity before finalizing the design in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What should I ask an ADU design contractor about utility upgrades and capacity before finalizing the design in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Utility capacity and routing can dramatically affect ADU cost and feasibility, yet many homeowners only discover issues after design is complete. In Los Angeles County, you should ask your ADU design contractor to evaluate utilities early. They should review your existing electrical panel size, main service capacity, water meter, sewer connection location, and gas service if applicable. For example, a 100-amp panel may not support both your main house and a fully electric ADU, making a panel or service upgrade likely. Ask the contractor to explain whether they anticipate upgrades and how those will be shown in the plans. Clarify who will coordinate with the local utility providers to confirm requirements and timelines. Trenching distances for water, sewer, and power can significantly increase costs, so request that your designer consider utility routes when proposing where to place the ADU on your lot. Have them highlight any need for sewer ejector pumps, backflow devices, or special drainage solutions. By including utility planning in early design decisions, you reduce the risk of surprise five-figure upgrades emerging once a builder bids the project or the city reviews your plans.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask your ADU design contractor to assess existing electrical, water, sewer, and gas capacity and distances, then design around realistic upgrade needs. Clarify who coordinates with utility providers, whether panel or service upgrades are expected, and how trenching routes and costs will affect ADU location and layout.
